identity: Sharp, with two tight turns linking two long straights
Sprints run on a straight course
layout: A sharp, right-handed track near Edinburgh where two tight turns link the back and home straights; the course was reconfigured to ease what was once Britain's tightest bend.
tactics: Balance matters, as at Chester; speedy horses that stay the trip usually do better than big gallopers on the round course.
A good turn of foot can open up a winning gap quickly.
Guides favour low draws on the round course up to about nine furlongs, and high draws on the straight course where fields group on the stands' rail.
ground: Good drainage keeps the going on the fast side, which helps speedier types.
guide_note: Low draws on the round course and high draws (stands' rail) on the straight course are the guide view; our draw figures check both.
